title: Custom theme `border.default`/`border.focused` are documented but ignored; explicit `DarkGray` is overridden when terminal background is detected

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue provides a clear, actionable bug report describing how documented custom theme border properties (`border.default` and `border.focused`) are ignored by `createCustomTheme` and overridden when terminal background detection is active, complete with detailed reproduction steps, investigation context, and environment details.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: Fixing the issue requires cross-package modifications spanning `packages/core` (updating `CustomTheme` schema interface) and `packages/cli` (updating `createCustomTheme` and `ThemeManager` color caching/resolution logic), as well as adding unit tests.

summary.problem: Custom theme border properties (`border.default` and `border.focused`) documented in docs/cli/themes.md are ignored during custom theme creation, and explicit border/DarkGray colors are unconditionally overridden when terminal background color detection (OSC 11) is active.
summary.root_cause: `createCustomTheme` in `theme.ts` does not read `customTheme.border` when building `semanticColors`, setting `semanticColors.border.default` directly to `colors.DarkGray`. Furthermore, `ThemeManager.getColors()` and `ThemeManager.getSemanticColors()` unconditionally recompute `DarkGray` and `border.default` based on `terminalBackground` interpolation, ignoring user-specified custom theme values.
summary.context: `CustomTheme` interface in `packages/core/src/config/config.ts` lacks `focused` property under `border`. Custom themes should be able to specify custom border colors that take precedence over automated terminal background color interpolation.

steps: Update `CustomTheme` interface in `packages/core/src/config/config.ts` to include `focused?: string` inside the `border` property.
Update `SemanticColors` interface in `packages/cli/src/ui/themes/semantic-tokens.ts` to include `focused?: string` inside `border`.
Modify `createCustomTheme` in `packages/cli/src/ui/themes/theme.ts` to assign `customTheme.border?.default` and `customTheme.border?.focused` to `semanticColors.border`.

Update `ThemeManager.getColors` and `ThemeManager.getSemanticColors` in `packages/cli/src/ui/themes/theme-manager.ts` so that custom theme border definitions and explicitly specified `DarkGray` values are preserved instead of being overridden by terminal background interpolation.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: Custom themes with defined `border.default` or `border.focused` properties (or explicit `DarkGray`) retain their specified border colors when rendered, even when a terminal background color is set.
verification_steps: Add unit test cases in `theme.test.ts` verifying that `createCustomTheme` correctly maps `customTheme.border.default` and `customTheme.border.focused` into `semanticColors.border`.
Add unit test cases in `theme-manager.test.ts` verifying that `ThemeManager.getSemanticColors()` returns custom border colors when terminal background color is set via `setTerminalBackground`.
